claims.statement: Sesam Hub is documented as a Master Data Hub for making up-to-date master data available in a data platform architecture.

This repository is the Sphinx product reference for documented configuration, data-processing semantics, APIs, tutorials, and operations, rather than the implementation of the processing runtime, Portal backend, or Management Studio; editing the reference does not implement a runtime fix.

Sphinx uses .rst authored sources and hub/index as its master document; the root index.rst is marked orphan and conf.py redirects index.html to hub/index.html, so the Markdown wiki is not the authored Sphinx entrypoint.
Management Studio configures, manages, and administers Sesam subscriptions and is accessed by selecting a subscription in the Sesam Portal, not by building this documentation.
Sesam consumes and produces streams of entities, which are JSON-like collections of key-value pairs with reserved property names.
Datasets are indexed entity logs used for storage, and content hashing appends an entity only when it is new or different from its previous version.

A pipe combines a source, transform chain, sink, and pump: the scheduled pump moves exposed entity streams through transformations to a sink, and DTL is the primary documented transform for joining and reshaping data.
System components represent external connections, centralize shared connection configuration, and provide services such as connection pooling and rate limiting.
The getting-started guide describes signup, connecting to a subscription, and baseline configuration, but its baseline-upload panel is commented out rather than an active third wizard step.
The signup tutorial describes requesting trial subscription access or obtaining an invitation from someone with management permissions for an existing subscription.

The first-synchronization tutorial still prescribes a HubSpot app developer account, test account, and API key with a legacydocs.hubspot.com link; those authored prerequisites should be qualified as dated instructions rather than verified current third-party setup.

The introductory Collect tutorial uses sesamcommunity/learn-sesam-crm:v1.1.2 for its Enhetsregisteret system and explicitly identifies that connection's data as generated mock test data rather than live register data.

The introductory synchronization exercise populates HubSpot with CRM data and later writes synchronized data back to HubSpot, so it should be approached as an exercise with external data side effects.
The documented ideal dataflow has five conceptual phases in order: Collect, Enrich, Connect, Transform, Share; these are conceptual steps rather than an exact five-pipe configuration requirement.
The Collect model retains raw source data, including an intermediary raw dataset to support replay or retention without requiring another external delivery.
Enrich adds business typing, namespaces, and relationship identifiers from the same source; cross-source relationships are deferred to Connect, where data is organized into global datasets.
Transform performs late schema binding from global datasets to the target schema in preparation pipes, while Share delivers data in the target's required form.

The introductory guide groups Collect and Share under Data Synchronization and Enrich, Connect, and Transform under Data Management, so its tutorial navigation differs from the conceptual five-phase processing order.

The documented local integration-test workflow drains pipe queues, disables or prevents outbound delivery to real systems, and compares endpoint pipe outputs with expected fixtures through the Sesam client.
A documented integration CI node must be unable to write to external systems, and tests sharing that node must run one at a time because the Sesam client overwrites node configuration.
The pump execution dataset logs execution history and read/write errors, but its entity ids and structure may change and it is explicitly not intended as a public application API.

The troubleshooting reference calls for separating entity and system failures, retaining target feedback, and monitoring or handling dead-letter data rather than treating every failed flow as a transformation defect.

README states a Python 3.7 minimum for pydata-sphinx-theme, while both PR and merge workflows select Python 3.9 on Ubuntu 22.04; this is version evidence for the documented build environment, not validation of arbitrary newer Python versions.

The documentation requirements directly pin Sphinx 4.5.0, docutils 0.16, pydata-sphinx-theme 0.8.0, sesamclient 0.2.68, and documentation extensions, rather than providing a fully locked transitive environment.

conf.py directly reads os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV'] when constructing exclusion patterns, so a missing variable can fail configuration loading with KeyError; local activation supplies it, whereas CI explicitly sets VIRTUAL_ENV to venv without an activation step.
README's local preview setup creates and activates .python_env, upgrades pip, installs wheel, and installs requirements.txt before building the site.

PR CI installs Pandoc 2.13 and texlive-latex-base, texlive-latex-extra, texlive-plain-generic, lmodern, texlive-fonts-recommended, and ghostscript for contract generation; README instead gives Ubuntu Pandoc/base/recommended LaTeX examples and a macOS brew install pandoc mactex example.

make html generates SaaS PDF/DOCX and partner DOCX downloads through Pandoc before running Sphinx into _build/html; its contract generation uses pagebreak.lua and PDF generation accounts for the documented LaTeX prerequisite.
The Makefile checks for sphinx-build on PATH and defaults SPHINXOPTS to -W, making Sphinx warnings build errors unless the options are overridden.

html_no_saas bypasses contract generation by touching the SaaS PDF/DOCX and partner DOCX paths and running the same HTML builder, not by filtering SaaS content; its recipe invokes neither Pandoc nor LaTeX, and touched missing downloads can be empty rather than freshly generated contracts.
README's SPHINXOPTS= make html_no_saas recommendation clears the Makefile's default -W as well as taking the contract-generation shortcut, so it is weaker than the configured PR build gate.
The documented HTML preview location is _build/html/index.html, and README offers cd _build/html && python3 -m http.server as an optional way to obtain search summaries.

The documentation PR workflow runs make html, not runtime integration tests, linkcheck, doctest, or coverage; the latter targets exist in Makefile, but conf.py does not enable the Sphinx doctest or coverage extensions.

On a push to master, merge CI builds HTML, packages and pushes documentation images, and deploys the SHA-tagged image to an Azure Container App; this publication workflow is distinct from local preview.
